connector: What is the most delicious thing you have ever tasted? Today Edmund tastes something he can't stop eating, and it changes his choices. Watch for each choice Edmund makes in Chapter 4, and what it leads to.

a.raw: the queen gives edmund a hot drink and he feels warm
a.fixed: The Queen gives Edmund a hot drink, and he feels warm.
a.why: The starts the sentence. Queen is used as her name, and Edmund is a name. A comma goes before and. Gives and feels are both present tense.

b.raw: edmund eats the turkish delight and he wants more
b.fixed: Edmund eats the Turkish Delight, and he wants more.
b.why: Edmund is a name. Turkish Delight is the name of a sweet. A comma goes before and. Eats and wants are both present tense.

mfill1.h1: The meaning says one shape. Type the root that means shape.
mfill1.why: uni + form = uniform: one shape for everyone.

mfill2.h1: To shape again. Which root means shape?
mfill2.why: re + form = reform: to shape again.

mfill3.h1: To change across. Look at the table for the root.
mfill3.why: trans + form = transform: to change shape.

mfill4.h1: Every word in the table hides the same root.
mfill4.why: in + form = inform: to shape what someone knows.

vcloze2.h1: The Queen means the lands she rules. Find that word.
vcloze2.why: Dominions are the lands someone rules.

vcloze3.h1: Lucy was very unhappy. Find the word for very unhappy.

cards.title: World Notes: Turkish Delight
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapter with your lens in mind.
text: Turkish delight is a real candy. It is soft and chewy, made with sugar and starch, and often dusted with powdered sugar.
It comes from Turkey, where people have made it for hundreds of years.
In the story, the Queen's Turkish Delight is enchanted. Real Turkish delight is just a sweet treat.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. Edmund tastes something he can't stop eating. Watch each choice he makes in Chapter 4, and what it leads to.
transcripts.guide1: Word work first: a root that means shape, verbs that stay in one time, and beats in long words.
transcripts.guide2: Read Chapter 4 with your lens. Then answer three questions.
transcripts.guide3: Today you draft a paragraph about a character's choice.

notes.wordParts: The root form means shape. uniform = one shape for everyone. transform = to change shape.
notes.grammar: Keep your verbs in the same time. If a story starts in the past (walked, ate), every verb stays in the past.
notes.spelling: Every beat in a word has one vowel sound. Count the sounds, not the letters: de-tail has two beats.
notes.wgrd: Name the choice, follow what happens because of it, and ask what the character knew when he chose.

mods.todo: Listen to Opti. Then tap the lens you will use today.
mods.script: [warmly] Here's this week's reading tip. In a story, almost nothing goes wrong by accident. Someone decides something first. Find the moment a character chooses, then follow what happens because of it. Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. The correct one first. The Queen smiles at Edmund, and she gives him a box of Turkish Delight. Smiles and gives are both happening now. Keep them in the same time. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Think about the question. Tap See what was hiding. Type the missing part of each word.
mods.script: [curious] Some word parts tell you about shape. Form means shape. Here's a word that's not on your list. Platform. Plat means flat. So a platform is a flat shape you stand on, like at a train station. Flat shape: platform! Read the four words and their parts. Then tap See what was hiding, and type the missing parts.

mods.todo: Fill in each sentence from the word bank. Tap Check My Work. Then play the matching game.
mods.script: Be a word detective with me. Superior. Here's the sentence. Edmund gave a very superior look, as if he were far older than Lucy. One, read the sentence: he's acting older and better. Two, look for word parts: super means above. Three, check it. Superior means acting as if you're above someone. Read how we figured out the first word. Then fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Last, play the matching game.

mods.todo: Tap Now check your thinking. Then tap every verb that slipped out of the past.
mods.script: [warmly] A story can happen in the past, or right now. Once you pick a time, the verbs stay there. Listen. Edmund climbed onto the sledge and sits down. Climbed is past. Sits is now! It slipped. It should be sat. Read The Rule box, and tap Now check your thinking. Then find every verb that slipped.

mods.todo: Clap the words. Tap See the Rule. Then sort all nine words by beats.
mods.script: Clap with me. Dan, ger, ous. Dangerous. Three claps! Each beat has one vowel sound. Now try beautiful. Beau, ti, ful. Beau has two vowel letters, but only one sound, so it's one beat. Count the sounds, not the letters. Clap the words in Group A and Group B, and tap See the Rule. Then sort the words.

mods.label: Opti shows you how
mods.todo: Write the sentence three new ways, one box at a time.
mods.script: [warmly] Here's copia: one idea, said many ways. Let me try a different sentence first. The dwarf bowed. Box one, change the opener: On the sledge, the dwarf bowed. Box two, a stronger verb: The dwarf bent low. Box three, add a detail: The fat dwarf bowed with a smile. Now it's your turn, one box at a time. If you get stuck, tap Show one way.

virtue.name: honesty
virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: Lucy tells Edmund all about the White Witch.
items.why: She tells him the truth about what she knows.

items.t: Edmund says, “I'm all right,” but the book says this was not true.
items.why: He was feeling very sick, and he hid it.

items.t: Edmund keeps it a secret that he has met the Queen.
items.why: Hiding what happened is not being honest.
